problem:
A supply pod of mass $30\,\text{kg}$ free-falls vertically downward. Let $v(t)$ be the pod's velocity, in meters per second, $t\ge 0$ seconds after the descent began, with downward taken as the positive direction.
The air resistance on the pod is proportional to its velocity with a constant of proportionality $k>0$ and acts in the direction opposite to motion.

Which differential equation best models the velocity? Assume that the acceleration due to gravity is $g,$ and the only forces acting on the pod are the weight due to gravity and drag.

activity_context.topic_title: Falling Body Problems With Linear Drag
